The Federal Ministry of Information reports Akwa Ibom State announced commencement of the electronic civil registration and vital statistics (e-CRVS) system for digital registration of births and deaths, replicating the NPC chairman's 15 July 2026 national briefing, with NPC asking the state to support full roll-out.

The article says Barnksforte Technologies Limited supports the development and deployment of the electronic civil registration and vital statistics system, with UNICEF providing technical, financial and technological support.
system: electronic civil registration and vital statistics system

fact: The NPC says its digitization includes mobile devices for real-time birth data collection, particularly in remote areas.

The NPC release says the First Lady's initiative supports birth registration using the national e-CRVS in all health facilities and communities, with symbolic electronic registration of children at the launch, where registrations were previously manual.
The NPC chairman said the e-CRVS system integrates birth registration with health facilities across several states, with over 15,000 children registered in Jigawa alone.

President Tinubu launched the VitalReg electronic civil registration and vital statistics system on 8 November 2023, implemented by the National Population Commission under a public-private partnership with Barnksforte Technologies and UNICEF support; no offices or coverage are stated.

NPC chairman Aminu Ibrahim Yusuf said digital birth and death registration on the VitalReg E-CRVS platform began on 1 July 2026 and is operational in all 36 states and the FCT, with paper forms no longer used.
NPC said deaths are registered in the same digital E-CRVS/VitalReg system, in operation since 1 July 2026.
NPC chairman said national birth registration coverage is about 57 percent and death registration below 20 percent, rates not tied to the digital system.
UNICEF says electronic birth registration is embedded in routine health care and operational in 14 states and the Federal Capital Territory, driving towards national coverage.
The World Bank's WDI lists completeness of birth registration in Nigeria at 42.6% for 2018, a national rate not tied to a digital system.

Nigeria 24 reports that the National Population Commission has launched VitalReg, a fully digital platform for birth registration replacing paper, usable through a self-service portal or any of 4,011 NPC centres across the 774 local government areas.
Nigeria 24 reports that VitalReg handles death and stillbirth notifications digitally, alongside birth registration.
Nigeria 24 states that roughly 43 per cent of annual births and over 80 per cent of deaths in Nigeria go unregistered, a national rate not tied to the digital system.

The e-CRVS platform was launched by President Tinubu on 8 November 2023, and the NPC says e-birth registration is rolling out state by state, already launched in Lagos (13 November 2025), Nasarawa, Kano, Borno and Enugu.
